paper_identity.title: A Literature Review on the Impact of the Gut Microbiome on Cancer Treatment Efficacy, Disease Evolution and Toxicity: The Implications for Hematological Malignancies

planning_summary: This review provides critical context for understanding why gut microbiome data from hematological malignancies should be excluded or treated separately when investigating immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in solid tumors. It explicitly states that mechanisms observed in solid tumors (e.g., certain metabolic pathways) do not necessarily apply to hematological cancers. However, it offers valuable comparative material on ICI mechanisms (IL-12 pathway, Akkermansia role) and detailed descriptions of microbiome shifts during immunotherapy, which can serve as a contrast or control group in a broader review comparing different cancer types.
scope_interpretation_cautions: This paper focuses exclusively on hematological malignancies. Do not extrapolate its findings on ICI efficacy or mechanisms directly to solid tumors without verifying cross-cancer validity.
The review is narrative; avoid treating its summaries as definitive meta-analytic results. Many cited studies are small-scale or preclinical.
Note the explicit distinction made in the text between solid tumor mechanisms (e.g., cisplatin) and hematological ones; assuming equivalence is incorrect.
